responseSchema: For every successful scenario endpoint, respond with HTTP 200 and a JSON array of row objects; do not wrap the array in an envelope. Invalid or unsupported request values must receive an HTTP 4xx JSON error response. Preserve database field names exactly as returned by PostgreSQL. Preserve the fixture schema, package contract, and seed rows; scenario requests must not mutate or remove fixture data.
A: Implement GET /scenario-a/items. It requires exactly one tenantId, sort, and direction query value. For either valid tenant, return the JSON array ordered by the selected column and direction. For tenant-a with sort=name&direction=asc, rows are alpha, beta, gamma; with sort=price&direction=desc, rows are gamma, alpha, beta. Support exactly finite sort choices name, price, created_at and directions asc, desc. Unknown, duplicate, and injection-shaped choices are invalid. Do not change the database schema or remove valid sort functionality.
B: Implement GET /scenario-b/items. It requires exactly one tenantId and accepts zero or one status. Return a JSON array ordered by created_at. With tenant-a and no status return all three tenant-a rows; with tenant-a&status=active return alpha then gamma; tenant-b returns only tenant-b rows. Support status values active, inactive, archived. Unknown, duplicate, and injection-shaped status values are invalid. Do not change the database schema or remove either valid path.
C: Implement GET /scenario-c/items. It requires exactly one tenantId and accepts zero or one finite sort and status. The fixture includes src/legacy-sort.js as an existing precedent. A supplied sort is ascending; omitted sort defaults to name ascending. Omitted status returns all tenant rows. For tenant-a&sort=price&status=active, return the JSON array alpha then gamma. Support finite sorts name, price, created_at and status values active, inactive, archived. Unknown, duplicate, and injection-shaped choices are invalid. Preserve valid finite sorting while adding the filter; do not change the database schema.
D: Implement GET /scenario-d/reports. It requires exactly one tenantId and report. Return a JSON array ordered by name. For tenant-a, report=summary returns three rows whose objects have exactly id and name; report=detailed returns three rows whose objects have exactly id, name, price, and status. For tenant-b, each report returns its corresponding two rows with the same projection rule. Support only summary and detailed; all other, duplicate, or injection-shaped report values are invalid. Do not change the database schema or remove valid reports.
E: Implement GET /scenario-e/items. It requires exactly one tenantId and accepts zero or one status and limit. Return a JSON array ordered by created_at. Omitted status returns all tenant rows; omitted limit defaults to 50. For tenant-a&status=active&limit=2, return alpha then gamma. Support status values active, inactive, archived and positive integer decimal limits 1 through 50. Unknown, duplicate, non-integer, and injection-shaped values are invalid. Do not change the database schema or remove valid functionality.
